description: One AI-generated practice set per grammar topic that had none (2026-10-13). Rules + an independent solver check; published right after import.

lessons.title: Personal Pronouns: I, you, he, she, it, we, they
lessons.description: You will practise choosing and using the pronouns I, you, he, she, it, we and they in short everyday sentences.

exercises.explanation: Sam is talking about himself, so he uses I with am.
exercises.prompt: My name is Sam. ___ am 16 years old.

exercises.explanation: Anna is a girl, so we use she.
exercises.prompt: Anna is my friend. ___ is very funny.

exercises.explanation: Tom is a boy, so we use he.
exercises.prompt: Tom plays football. ___ is fast.

exercises.explanation: A phone is a thing, so we use it.
exercises.prompt: This is my phone. ___ is new. (he, she or it)

exercises.explanation: Maria is a girl, so we must say She, not He.
exercises.prompt: “Maria is my sister. He is 14.” is a correct sentence.

exercises.explanation: Ben and I includes the speaker, so we use we.
exercises.prompt: Ben and I are in the same class. ___ are friends. (I, we or they)

exercises.explanation: Lisa and Kate are two other people, so we use they.
exercises.prompt: Lisa and Kate love music. ___ sing every day.

exercises.explanation: We use he for a boy, she for a girl, it for an animal, we with me, and they for other people.
exercises.prompt: Match the names with the correct pronoun.

exercises.explanation: The sentence starts with the pronoun They, then are, then the place.
The speaker asks Mia, so we use you.
exercises.prompt: Hi Mia, how are ___ today? (I or you)

exercises.explanation: We goes with are, so the correct sentence is We are at home.
exercises.prompt: “We is at home.” is a correct sentence.

exercises.explanation: A normal sentence starts with She and I, then are, then best friends.

lessons.title: My, Your, His, Her: Possessive Adjectives
lessons.description: Practise using my, your, his, her, its, our and their to show who owns something.

exercises.explanation: I goes with my.
exercises.prompt: I love music. ___ phone is full of songs.

exercises.explanation: You goes with your.
exercises.prompt: You have a new bag. ___ bag is cool.

exercises.explanation: Tom is a boy, so we use his.
exercises.prompt: Tom is my friend. ___ phone is red. (Tom)

exercises.explanation: Anna is a girl, so we use her.
exercises.prompt: Anna is my sister. ___ hair is long. (Anna)

exercises.explanation: For a boy we say his, not her.
exercises.prompt: “He likes her new game” is correct when the game belongs to a boy named Sam.

exercises.explanation: We goes with our.
exercises.prompt: My friends and I love pizza. ___ favourite food is pizza.

exercises.explanation: The possessive adjective Their comes before the noun teacher.
Max and Leo are they, so we use their.
exercises.prompt: Max and Leo play football. ___ team is great. (Max and Leo)

exercises.explanation: Each person word has its own possessive adjective.
exercises.prompt: Match the person with the correct word.

exercises.explanation: We goes with our.
exercises.prompt: “We love our school” is a correct sentence.

exercises.explanation: For an animal or thing we use its.
exercises.prompt: The dog is happy. ___ ball is under the bed. (the dog)

exercises.explanation: Mia and I is we, so we use our.
exercises.prompt: Mia and I are in a band. ___ band is called Blue Sky.

lessons.title: This, That, These, Those
lessons.description: You will practise using this, that, these and those for things near you and far from you, one and more than one.

exercises.explanation: One thing near you is this.
exercises.prompt: I have a phone in my hand. ___ is my phone.

exercises.explanation: One thing far from you is that.
exercises.prompt: Look at the bus over there. ___ is my bus.

exercises.explanation: Two things near you are these.
exercises.prompt: I have two new shoes here. ___ are my new shoes.

exercises.explanation: More than one thing far from you is those.
exercises.prompt: Look at the two boys over there. ___ are my friends.

exercises.explanation: One thing near you is this.
exercises.prompt: I am holding a cup of coffee. ___ is my coffee.

exercises.explanation: Many things far from you are those.
exercises.prompt: Look at the three cars over there. ___ are very fast.

exercises.explanation: These is for more than one thing, so we say these are or this is.
exercises.prompt: “These is my bag” is a correct sentence.

exercises.explanation: Those goes with are for more than one thing.
exercises.prompt: “Those are my headphones” is a correct sentence.

exercises.explanation: We say That is and then the thing.
These goes with are and a plural noun.
This and these are near; that and those are far; this and that are for one thing.
exercises.prompt: Match the sentence start with the correct ending.

exercises.explanation: Dogs is more than one and they are far, so we use those.
exercises.prompt: Look at the two dogs over there. ___ dogs are big.

lessons.title: Have Got: Things We Own
lessons.description: You will practise have got and has got in positive sentences, negatives and questions.

exercises.explanation: We use have got with I.
exercises.prompt: I ___ got a new phone.

exercises.explanation: We use has got with she.
exercises.prompt: She ___ got a big family.

exercises.explanation: We use have got with we.
exercises.prompt: We ___ got a cool teacher. (have or has)

exercises.explanation: My brother means he, so we use has got.
exercises.prompt: My brother ___ got a red bike. (have or has)

exercises.explanation: With he we say has got, not have got.
exercises.prompt: “He have got a dog” is a correct sentence.

exercises.explanation: The negative with they is haven't got.
exercises.prompt: They ___ got a car.

exercises.explanation: The negative with Tom (he) is hasn't got.
exercises.prompt: Tom ___ got a laptop. He uses his phone. (negative: has or have)

exercises.explanation: The order is subject, have got, then the thing.
In a question, Have comes first, then the subject, then got.
The question with she begins with Has.
exercises.prompt: ___ she got a headphones case? No, she hasn't.

exercises.explanation: Your friend means he or she, so Has is correct.
exercises.prompt: “Has your friend got a skateboard?” is a correct question.

exercises.explanation: The short answer uses the same have or has as the question.
exercises.prompt: Match the questions with the short answers.

lessons.title: Imperatives: Giving Instructions
lessons.description: You will practise using imperatives to give instructions, make requests and say what not to do.

exercises.explanation: An imperative uses the base form of the verb.
exercises.prompt: ___ the door, please.

exercises.explanation: We use the base form, Turn off, to give an instruction.
exercises.prompt: ___ your phone in class, please.

exercises.explanation: The imperative is the base form of the verb: Sit.
exercises.prompt: ___ (sit) down, please.

exercises.explanation: The imperative has no -s: Open your book.
exercises.prompt: “Opens your book” is a correct imperative.

exercises.explanation: After Don't we use the base form: be.
exercises.prompt: Don't ___ late for the party!

exercises.explanation: A negative imperative is Don't plus the base verb.
exercises.prompt: ___ (not, run) in the school, please. Use: Don't ...

exercises.explanation: An imperative starts with the verb: Listen to this song.
After Don't we use the base form: Don't talk.
exercises.prompt: “Don't talks in the library” is a correct sentence.

exercises.explanation: The order is Please, Don't, verb, then the object.
Each instruction fits only one place.
exercises.prompt: Match the instruction with the place.

exercises.explanation: We say Don't plus the base verb to tell someone not to do something.
exercises.prompt: Ben is tired. ___ (not, wake) him up, please. Use: Don't ...

exercises.explanation: Loud means we want less sound, so we say Turn down with the base form.
exercises.prompt: The video is too loud. ___ the volume, please.

lessons.title: In, On, At: Time and Place
lessons.description: You will practise using in, on and at to talk about time and place.

exercises.explanation: We use at with clock times.
exercises.prompt: My class starts ___ 9 o'clock.

exercises.explanation: We use on with days.
exercises.prompt: I have a party ___ Saturday.

exercises.explanation: We use in with months.
exercises.prompt: My birthday is ___ July.

exercises.explanation: We use at with clock times.
exercises.prompt: I get up ___ 7 o'clock.

exercises.explanation: We use on with days.
exercises.prompt: We play games ___ Friday.

exercises.explanation: We say on Monday, not in Monday.
exercises.prompt: "I go to school in Monday" is a correct sentence.

exercises.explanation: The phone is on top of the table, so we use on.
exercises.prompt: My phone is ___ the table.

exercises.explanation: The keys are inside the bag, so we use in.
exercises.prompt: My keys are ___ my bag.

exercises.explanation: We use in with parts of the day like the evening.
We use at with school as a place.
exercises.prompt: "We are at school now" is a correct sentence.

exercises.explanation: The place with at comes first, then the day with on.

lessons.title: Question Words: What, Where, When, Who, Why, How
lessons.description: You will practise asking questions with what, where, when, who, why, how, whose and how many.

exercises.explanation: London is a place, so we ask Where.
exercises.prompt: ___ do you live? I live in London.

exercises.explanation: May is a time, so we ask When.
exercises.prompt: ___ is your birthday? It is in May. (what, when or where)

exercises.explanation: We use Who to ask about a person.
exercises.prompt: ___ is that boy? He is my brother.

exercises.explanation: Where asks about places.
exercises.prompt: We use Where to ask about a place.

exercises.explanation: The answer gives a reason with Because, so we ask Why.
exercises.prompt: ___ are you sad? Because I lost my phone. (what, why or who)

exercises.explanation: Each question word asks for a different kind of answer: place, time, person, reason.
exercises.prompt: Match each question with its answer.

exercises.explanation: The order is question word, do, subject, verb.
By bus tells us the way, so we ask How.
exercises.prompt: ___ do you go to school? I go by bus.

exercises.explanation: Five is a number of books, so we ask How many.
exercises.prompt: ___ books do you have? I have five. (how many or how much)

exercises.explanation: We need do: When do you like music? or better, What music do you like?
exercises.prompt: “When you like music?” is a correct question.

exercises.explanation: We say What time, then does, then the subject and the verb.

lessons.title: Object Pronouns: me, you, him, her, it, us, them
lessons.description: You will practise using object pronouns like me, him, us and them after verbs and prepositions.

exercises.explanation: After the verb give we use the object pronoun me.
exercises.prompt: My friend is calling. Please give ___ my phone.

exercises.explanation: Sara is a girl, and her is the object pronoun after the verb text.
exercises.prompt: Sara is my best friend. I text ___ every day.

exercises.explanation: The object form of he is him.
exercises.prompt: Tom is funny. I really like ___ (he).

exercises.explanation: After the verb call we need me, not I.
exercises.prompt: “Call I tonight” is a correct sentence.

exercises.explanation: Each subject pronoun has its own object pronoun.
exercises.prompt: Match the subject pronoun with the object pronoun.

exercises.explanation: The object form of they is them.
exercises.prompt: My parents are at home. I will call ___ (they) after school.

exercises.explanation: The object pronoun me comes after the verb send.
After the preposition with we use us.
exercises.prompt: Come to the cinema with ___. We have two tickets.

exercises.explanation: It comes after the verb play, so it is the object.
exercises.prompt: “This game is great. I play it every day.” In this sentence, “it” is an object pronoun.

exercises.explanation: The object form of we is us.
exercises.prompt: Anna and I are new here. Can you help ___ (we), please?

exercises.explanation: The pronoun us comes right after the verb gave.
Mia and Leo are two people, and after next to we use them.
exercises.prompt: Mia and Leo are waiting. Let's sit next to ___.

lessons.title: Was or Were? Talking About the Past
lessons.description: You will practise using was and were to talk about people, places and feelings in the past.

exercises.explanation: We use was with I in the past.
exercises.prompt: Yesterday I ___ at home.

exercises.explanation: We use were with they in the past.
exercises.prompt: They ___ at the cinema last night.

exercises.explanation: We use was with she in the past.
exercises.prompt: She ___ happy after the party last Friday.

exercises.explanation: We use were with we in the past.
exercises.prompt: We ___ tired after the football game yesterday.

exercises.explanation: The correct form is “You were late”, because we use were with you.
exercises.prompt: “You was late for class” is a correct sentence.

exercises.explanation: Phone is one thing, so we use was.
exercises.prompt: My phone ___ on the table ten minutes ago.

exercises.explanation: The subject comes first, then were, then the place.
In a question, were comes before the subject.
Pizzas is plural, so the negative is weren't or were not.
exercises.prompt: The pizzas ___ not very good, so we didn't eat them. (negative, short form)

exercises.explanation: Brothers is plural, so the correct question is “Were your brothers at the game?”
exercises.prompt: “Was your brothers at the game?” is a correct question.
